title: Only 8% Pass This Paramedic Entrance Exam
summary: Read the scene, notice changing observations and connect the clues under pressure.

landing.intro:
Read the clues. Make the connections.
Put your thinking to the test.

about.body:
Explore body systems, scene awareness, observations, communication and practical reasoning. Each set brings a different kind of emergency-care clue into focus.

Choose the answer supported by the information shown. Checkpoints describe your performance on the topic just completed, followed by an overall result and optional answer review.

Questions avoid local emergency numbers, medication doses, clinical algorithms and country-specific professional powers. This entertainment quiz is not an accredited entrance exam, practical assessment or instruction for treating a real emergency.

steps: Read the clues and choose one answer.
See your topic profile at each checkpoint and continue to a new challenge.
Reveal your overall result, then optionally review the answers you missed.

about.disclaimer: For entertainment and general learning only. This is not an accredited paramedic entrance examination, clinical assessment, professional qualification or medical advice. Emergency procedures and responsibilities vary; always follow local guidance and appropriately qualified emergency professionals.

paramedic-s1q1.question: Which gas does blood pick up in the lungs?

paramedic-s1q2.question: Which organs remove wastes from blood and help regulate water balance?

paramedic-s1q3.question: Which system carries rapid signals between the brain and the body?

paramedic-s1q4.question: Where are most digested nutrients absorbed?

paramedic-s1q5.question: Which blood cells carry most of the oxygen in blood?

paramedic-s1q6.question: Which major muscle helps draw air into the lungs?

paramedic-s1q7.question: Which heart chamber receives blood returning from the lungs?

paramedic-s2q1.question: A live electrical cable blocks the doorway. What comes first?

answers.a1: Step over it while carrying equipment
answers.a2: Keep clear and obtain qualified help to make the area safe
answers.a3: Move it with an ordinary household object
answers.a4: Ask an untrained bystander to hold it away

paramedic-s2q2.question: A person is beside moving traffic with no protected working area. What is safest?

answers.a1: Keep clear and arrange appropriate scene support
answers.a3: Assume drivers have already seen everyone
answers.a4: Place a bag in the lane as the only barrier

paramedic-s2q3.question: Smoke begins to block an exit that was clear earlier. What matters now?

answers.a1: Ignore the smoke until paperwork is complete
answers.a2: Treat the original plan as unchangeable
answers.a3: Reassess safety and seek appropriate support
answers.a4: Rely only on the earlier safe assessment

paramedic-s2q4.question: Used needles and broken glass lie on the floor. What is the safe initial response?

answers.a2: Keep people away and arrange safe removal
answers.a4: Pick them up with bare hands

paramedic-s2q5.question: A strong fuel smell is present after a vehicle collision. What does it indicate?

answers.a1: A reason to use a flame for a closer look
answers.a2: A potential hazard requiring scene precautions
answers.a3: Proof that no fire risk exists

paramedic-s2q6.question: A person at the scene becomes violent and blocks the approach. What is appropriate?

answers.a2: Ignore the threat because a task is waiting
answers.a3: Keep a safe distance and request suitable support
answers.a4: Ask a bystander to restrain them without help

paramedic-s2q7.question: Why should scene safety be reassessed as an incident develops?

answers.a2: A safe entrance guarantees every later area is safe

paramedic-s3q1.question: A pulse changes from 72 to 88 beats per minute. What does the record show?

answers.a1: An increase of 16 beats per minute
answers.a2: An increase of 8 beats per minute
answers.a3: A decrease of 16 beats per minute

paramedic-s3q2.question: Earlier, a person spoke comfortably. Now they pause between short phrases to breathe. What changed?

answers.a1: The record proves a specific diagnosis

paramedic-s3q3.question: Which observation describes a new change in alertness?

answers.a1: The chart has a new page
answers.a4: The room lights were switched on

paramedic-s3q4.question: Which description records a breathing rate?

paramedic-s3q5.question: What does a pulse oximeter estimate?

paramedic-s3q6.question: Why should a reassuring device reading not replace assessment of new symptoms?

answers.a1: One number proves all body systems are healthy
answers.a2: Measurements have limitations and need context
answers.a4: Every device always gives random values

paramedic-s3q7.question: Which change calls for prompt qualified assessment?

answers.a2: New breathing difficulty with reduced alertness
answers.a4: A different pen used for notes

paramedic-s4q1.question: A record shows 750 mL plus 250 mL. What is the total?

paramedic-s4q2.question: How many millilitres are in 1.5 L?

paramedic-s4q3.question: How much time passes from 09:20 to 10:05?

paramedic-s4q4.question: You count 9 breaths in 30 seconds. What is the equivalent rate per minute?

paramedic-s4q5.question: A recorded total rises from 600 mL to 900 mL. What is the percentage increase?

paramedic-s4q6.question: Divide 1.2 L equally across four recorded periods. How much belongs to each?

paramedic-s4q7.question: Three sealed boxes hold eight items each. How many items are there?

paramedic-s5q1.question: A person says, “I’m worried about what happens next.” What is the best opening?

answers.a3: Promise there is no possible risk
answers.a4: Acknowledge the worry and invite questions

paramedic-s5q2.question: Someone wants to discuss a sensitive concern in a busy public area. What protects privacy?

answers.a2: Write the details on a public board

paramedic-s5q3.question: A person has not understood an explanation. What helps check understanding?

answers.a1: Explain plainly and ask them to describe it in their own words
answers.a2: Treat a nod as proof of understanding
answers.a4: Ask another patient to answer for them

paramedic-s5q4.question: Before a non-urgent examination, what should the person receive?

answers.a1: An assurance that questions are not allowed
answers.a2: Only a form with no explanation
answers.a3: A clear explanation and an opportunity to consent
answers.a4: A decision made by the nearest visitor

paramedic-s5q5.question: A person declines having students present. What is the respectful response?

answers.a2: Respect the choice and protect privacy
answers.a3: Assume silence later cancels the choice

paramedic-s5q6.question: A language barrier makes an important discussion difficult. What is the best support?

answers.a2: Asking a young child to interpret sensitive details

paramedic-s5q7.question: A person with hearing difficulty asks you to repeat yourself. What is helpful?

answers.a4: Face them and check their preferred way to communicate

paramedic-s6q1.question: Which tool is designed to measure body temperature?

paramedic-s6q2.question: Which instrument is used to listen to body sounds?

paramedic-s6q3.question: Which device uses an inflatable cuff to help measure blood pressure?

paramedic-s6q4.question: A task risks splashing body fluid into the eyes. What protection addresses that risk?

paramedic-s6q5.question: A sterile dressing packet is damaged. What is the safe decision?

answers.a1: Do not assume the dressing remains sterile
answers.a2: Use it because the label is readable
answers.a3: Ignore the damage if the packet is dry
answers.a4: Tape the outside and call it sterile

paramedic-s6q6.question: Why check equipment before it is needed?

answers.a1: To avoid checking instructions for unfamiliar equipment
answers.a2: To identify missing items or faults early
answers.a3: To guarantee it can never fail later

paramedic-s6q7.question: A device displays an error message. What should guide the response?

answers.a1: The instructions and an appropriate assessment of the situation
answers.a2: Treating the error as a normal patient value
answers.a3: Guessing from the screen colour alone

paramedic-s7q1.question: A note says “left arm” but the handover says “right arm”. What needs clarification?

paramedic-s7q2.question: A measurement is written as “12” with no unit. What is missing?

answers.a4: The unit needed to interpret the value

paramedic-s7q3.question: Which record clearly separates a reported symptom from an observation?

answers.a1: “Nothing happened because the chart is blank”
answers.a3: “Definitely has a diagnosis I have not assessed”

paramedic-s7q4.question: Why include the time beside a new observation?

answers.a2: To place it in the sequence of events
answers.a3: To prove the cause by itself

paramedic-s7q5.question: A chart has no entry for a scheduled measurement. What can you conclude?

paramedic-s7q6.question: Which entry records what happened most clearly?

paramedic-s7q7.question: Why compare current observations with earlier ones?

answers.a3: To avoid looking at the person
answers.a4: To prove a diagnosis from any difference

paramedic-s8q1.question: In the WHO Basic Emergency Care ABCDE approach, what does A refer to?

paramedic-s8q2.question: In that ABCDE approach, what does B refer to?

paramedic-s8q3.question: In that ABCDE approach, what does C refer to?

answers.a1: Whether the person responds to a spoken question
answers.a3: The date on a wall calendar
answers.a4: The colour of the equipment bag

paramedic-s8q5.question: Why can ineffective breathing affect body tissues?

answers.a4: Less oxygen may reach the blood and tissues

paramedic-s8q6.question: What does circulation transport to body tissues?

paramedic-s8q7.question: Why does sudden reduced alertness deserve attention?

answers.a2: It rules out a breathing problem
answers.a4: It may signal a serious change needing assessment

paramedic-s9q1.question: Which first message gives responders the clearest useful scene picture?

answers.a2: “Please come; the colour of the vehicle is blue”
answers.a3: “The scene is difficult; I have no details”
answers.a4: “River Gate: two people, smoke present, access blocked”

paramedic-s9q2.question: A critical instruction is hard to hear over noise. What should the receiver do?

answers.a1: Ask for clarification and repeat back the key details
answers.a3: Replace it with a different instruction

paramedic-s9q3.question: A new urgent concern develops during a routine equipment check. What should guide the priority?

answers.a3: The immediate risk and the need for qualified help
answers.a4: The order written on an old list

paramedic-s9q4.question: Several people assume someone else has requested help. What is missing?

answers.a1: Clear assignment and confirmation of the task
answers.a2: A new colour for the radio
answers.a4: A longer list of unrelated facts

paramedic-s9q5.question: A colleague reports a sudden change. What makes the handover more useful?

answers.a1: Ask what changed, when and what was observed
answers.a2: Ignore it because the person was stable earlier
answers.a4: Ask only about the room number

paramedic-s9q6.question: A task requires skills you do not have. What is appropriate?

answers.a1: Use an unrelated technique from memory
answers.a2: Attempt it because someone is watching
answers.a3: Ask an untrained bystander to perform it
answers.a4: Request qualified assistance and follow the relevant guidance

paramedic-s9q7.question: Two sources give conflicting incident times. What should be recorded?

answers.a1: A guessed time presented as certain
answers.a2: The discrepancy and the need to clarify it

paramedic-s10q1.question: Person A has a sore wrist and speaks normally. Person B is newly confused and struggling to breathe. Who needs urgent attention?

answers.a2: Person A because the wrist is visible
answers.a3: Whichever person is closest to a chair
answers.a4: Neither until a diagnosis is confirmed

paramedic-s10q2.question: A call is logged at 14:35 and arrival is at 15:12. How much time has passed?

paramedic-s10q3.question: Breathing becomes faster while the person becomes harder to engage. Which conclusion is supported?

answers.a1: No concern exists without a device reading
answers.a3: There is deterioration needing prompt qualified assessment

paramedic-s10q4.question: A route becomes unsafe while a person needs assistance. Which response considers both needs?

answers.a1: Send an untrained bystander into the danger
answers.a2: Use the unsafe route regardless of the hazard
answers.a3: Reassess the route and arrange appropriate help
answers.a4: Ignore the new hazard because the task began earlier

paramedic-s10q5.question: A record contains 0.65 L plus 350 mL. What is the combined volume?

paramedic-s10q6.question: Which sentence distinguishes an observation from an unconfirmed cause?

answers.a1: “The person is confused because they are difficult”
answers.a2: “New confusion began at 10:20; the cause is not yet established”
answers.a3: “No confirmed cause means the change is harmless”

paramedic-s10q7.question: A scene update reports a blocked exit and a person becoming less responsive. Which handover preserves both priorities?

answers.a1: Omit both until a diagnosis is confirmed
answers.a3: Report the access hazard and the person’s deterioration
answers.a4: Report only the original safe route
